name: Automic Vault
category: Local execution security and secrets management
title: A security boundary for CLI tools
description: Automic Vault removes plaintext secrets from CLI tools and controls which signed apps can use them beneath the agent harness.
promises: Removes credentials from dotfiles and tool configs.
Gives credentials only to the right executable.
Applies one local boundary to every launcher.

risk_story.eyebrow: A prompt cannot protect a secret the agent can already read
risk_story.failure: An agent found a reusable cloud credential and uploaded it to a remote server.
risk_story.controlled: Automic Vault moves credentials out of readable tool configs, then checks the executable, signed launcher, command, working directory, and requested key before use.

approval_controls_heading: Policy follows the tool and its launcher.

approval_controls.description: The app gets no automatic access. Every request requires approval.
For tools you trust somewhat, like agents. Safe reads can proceed; writes require approval.
For a terminal where you never intend to run npm i. Commands that could reveal secrets always keep an approval gate.
approval_controls.footnote: Installed packages must cross the same boundary to use protected secrets. Supply-chain attacks such as the 2025 Shai-Hulud npm worm target credentials available to developer tools. Defense in depth still matters: run npm i in a dedicated terminal with low-to-no privileges in both Automic Vault and macOS TCC.

audit_log.description: Every approved or denied, automatic or manual secret request leaves a local record.

threat_monitoring.mitigation: Each finding includes clear steps to mitigate it.

terminal_security.problem: Command-line tools usually run with the authority of the app that launched them, such as Terminal, an AI harness, an editor, or an automation app.
terminal_security.control: Automic Vault identifies the tool and its signed launcher, then applies access rules to that pairing.
